HomePage.title: Convert your files without them ever leaving your computer
HomePage.tagline: Images and PDFs are processed right in your browser: faster, more private and free. No watermarks, no account needed.

privacy.title: Actually private
privacy.body: Your images and PDFs are never uploaded — everything happens on your device.

speed.title: Seriously fast
speed.body: No waiting for uploads or downloads. Conversion starts instantly.

free.title: Free, no sign-up
free.body: No watermarks, no mandatory accounts and no hidden limits.

office.title: Office documents too
office.body: Word, Excel and PowerPoint are converted on our server and deleted within 1 hour.

HomePage.badge: Your files never leave your device

how.heading: How it works
how.subtitle: Three steps, nothing to install and no account needed.

drop.title: Drop your file
drop.body: Drop images or PDFs on the area above, or tap it to pick them. You can add several at once.

pick.title: Pick a format
pick.body: Choose the output format and, if you like, adjust the quality or size.

download.title: Download the result
download.body: The conversion runs on your device in seconds. Download each file or all of them in a ZIP.

free.a: Yes. You can convert without paying, without an account and without watermarks. The Pro plan is optional: it removes ads and raises the limits.

upload.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
upload.a: Images and PDFs are processed right in your browser and never leave your device. Only office documents (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) are converted on our server, and they are deleted within 1 hour.

formats.a: JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO, HEIC and SVG images; tools to merge, split, rotate, organize and compress PDFs; images to PDF and PDF to image; and Word, Excel and PowerPoint documents to PDF.

mobile.q: Does it work on my phone?
mobile.a: Yes. Fileflect works in your phone or tablet browser, with no app to install. For example, you can turn iPhone HEIC photos into JPG.

batch.q: Can I convert several files at once?
batch.a: Yes. Add several files at once and download them one by one or all together in a ZIP file.

quality.a: You decide: you can adjust the quality of compressed formats (JPG, WEBP, AVIF). Lossless formats such as PNG keep the image exactly as it is.

merge-pdf.title: Merge PDF
merge-pdf.description: Combine several PDFs into one, in any order. Your files are never uploaded.
merge-pdf.about: Merge PDF joins several documents into a single file. You can change the order with the move up and move down buttons before merging. Pages are copied as they are: text, links and image quality don't change.

faq.q1: Do I lose quality when merging PDFs?
faq.a1: No. Pages are copied without being recompressed, so text stays selectable and images keep their resolution.
faq.q2: Can I choose the order of the files?
faq.a2: Yes. Use each file's move up and move down buttons; the final PDF follows the order of the list.
faq.q3: Can I merge password-protected PDFs?
faq.a3: No. An encrypted PDF can't be read without its password; you'll see a warning and can remove it from the list.

split-pdf.title: Split PDF
split-pdf.description: Split a PDF into several files or extract just the pages you need.
split-pdf.about: Split PDF separates a document into several files. You can save each page as its own PDF, make one PDF per range (for example 1-3, 4-6) or extract just some pages into a single file. When the result has several PDFs, they download together as a ZIP.

faq.q1: How do I write page ranges?
faq.a1: Separate ranges with commas: 1-3, 5, 8-. A single number is one page and "8-" means from page 8 to the end.
faq.q2: Can I take out just a few pages without splitting everything?
faq.a2: Yes. Choose "Extract pages into one PDF" and type the pages you want to keep.
faq.q3: Is the original PDF changed?
faq.a3: No. Fileflect creates new files and your original PDF stays the same on your device.

rotate-pdf.title: Rotate PDF
rotate-pdf.description: Turn the pages of a PDF and save it the right way up.
rotate-pdf.about: Rotate PDF turns pages 90° clockwise, 90° counterclockwise or 180°. You can rotate every page or only the ones you list, such as scanned pages that came out upside down. The rotation is saved in the file, so it looks right in any reader.

faq.q1: Can I rotate only some pages?
faq.a1: Yes. Choose "Only some" and type the pages or ranges, for example 2, 5-7.
faq.q2: Does rotating a PDF reduce quality?
faq.a2: No. Only the page orientation changes; the content isn't recompressed.
faq.q3: Does the rotation stay when I open it in another app?
faq.a3: Yes. The rotation is saved in the PDF and is respected by Acrobat, web browsers and phone readers.

organize-pdf.title: Organize PDF pages
organize-pdf.description: Reorder, rotate or delete PDF pages with thumbnails.
organize-pdf.about: Organize PDF shows a thumbnail of every page so you can rearrange the document visually: drag pages to their new place (or use the buttons), rotate the ones that need it and delete the ones you don't want. When you're done, you download a new PDF in the chosen order.

faq.q1: Can I use it without a mouse?
faq.a1: Yes. Each page has buttons to move it earlier or later, rotate it and delete it, usable with the keyboard and on touch screens.
faq.q2: I deleted a page by mistake. Can I get it back?
faq.a2: Yes. The "Restore all" button brings back the original document before you download.
faq.q3: Does it work with long PDFs?
faq.a3: Yes, although thumbnails take longer to generate for long or image-heavy documents, especially on phones.

images-to-pdf.title: Images to PDF
images-to-pdf.description: Turn JPG, PNG, HEIC and other photos into a single PDF.
images-to-pdf.about: Images to PDF creates a document with one image per page. It accepts JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO, HEIC (iPhone photos) and SVG. You can reorder the images, choose the page size (same as the image, A4 or Letter) and a margin; photos are turned according to their EXIF orientation.

faq.q1: Can I turn iPhone photos (HEIC) into a PDF?
faq.a1: Yes. HEIC photos are decoded in your browser and added to the PDF like any other image.
faq.q2: Which page size should I pick?
faq.a2: "Same as image" adds no borders. A4 or Letter are good for printing or sending documents: the image is centered and fitted without stretching.
faq.q3: What if an image is damaged?
faq.a3: You'll see a warning with the name of the file that failed so you can remove or replace it; your other images are kept.

compress-pdf.title: Compress PDF
compress-pdf.description: Make your PDFs smaller to send them by email or WhatsApp.
compress-pdf.about: Compress PDF makes the file smaller by re-encoding the photos inside it, which are usually why a PDF is heavy. Text, fonts and vector drawings are kept as they are. There are three levels: low (best quality), recommended and strong (smallest file).

faq.q1: Why did my PDF barely shrink?
faq.a1: If the PDF is mostly text, or its images are already optimized, there's little to reduce. In that case Fileflect tells you instead of giving you a bigger file.
faq.q2: Does the text get blurry?
faq.a2: No. Only images are recompressed; text stays sharp, selectable and searchable.
faq.q3: Which level should I pick for email or WhatsApp?
faq.a3: Recommended is usually enough. If the file is still large, try strong: photos lose some detail but the document stays readable.

json-to-csv.title: JSON to CSV
json-to-csv.description: Convert JSON into a CSV or TSV table for Excel or Google Sheets. Your data is never uploaded.
json-to-csv.about: JSON to CSV turns a list of JSON objects into a table: each object becomes a row and each key a column. Nested objects become dotted columns (for example address.city) and lists become numbered columns (tags.0, tags.1). Choose comma, semicolon or tab (TSV), and add the UTF-8 mark so Excel shows accented characters correctly.

faq.q1: Which JSON does it accept?
faq.a1: A list of objects, a single object, an object wrapping a single list (like '{'"items": [...]'}') or a list of lists, which is written as rows as is. If the JSON has a syntax error you will see a warning.
faq.q2: Why does Excel show broken accents or everything in one column?
faq.a2: Keep the Excel-compatible option checked (it adds the UTF-8 mark). If your Excel uses a comma as the decimal separator, as in much of Europe and Latin America, choose semicolon.
faq.q3: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a3: No. The conversion runs in your browser, in the background, and the file never leaves your device.

csv-to-json.title: CSV to JSON
csv-to-json.description: Convert CSV or TSV into JSON with automatic delimiter detection. Your data is never uploaded.
csv-to-json.about: CSV to JSON reads a table with a header row and produces a list of JSON objects, one per row. It detects whether the file uses commas, semicolons, tabs or pipes, keeps quotes and line breaks inside cells, and reads files saved by Excel in UTF-8 or Windows-1252. Optionally it converts numbers and true/false, and rebuilds objects from dotted columns.

faq.q1: How are numbers handled?
faq.a1: With value conversion on, a number is written as a number only if it reads back the same: 007 or a 20-digit number stay as text so no zeros or precision are lost. Empty cells become null.
faq.q2: What about empty or repeated headers?
faq.a2: They get a name of their own (column3, name_2) so no column is lost. Rows with fewer cells are filled with null.
faq.q3: Can I get nested objects?
faq.a3: Yes. Columns like address.city or tags.0 become objects and lists. If a column clashes with another one, it is kept as is so no data is lost.

json-to-yaml.title: JSON to YAML
json-to-yaml.description: Convert JSON into readable YAML for config files, Kubernetes or CI. In your browser.
json-to-yaml.about: JSON to YAML rewrites your JSON data as block-indented YAML, easier to read and edit by hand in config files, Kubernetes manifests, docker-compose files or CI pipelines. Strings an older YAML reader would take as something else (yes, no, on, 007, dates) are quoted so they keep their type.

faq.q1: Why are some values quoted?
faq.a1: Because without quotes some YAML 1.1 readers would read them differently: yes and on as true, 007 as a number or 2020-01-01 as a date. Quotes make sure they stay text.
faq.q2: Are order and types kept?
faq.a2: Yes. Keys keep their order, and numbers, booleans and null are written with their YAML type. Long lines are not wrapped.
faq.q3: Can I convert several files at once?
faq.a3: Yes. Pick several .json files and download each YAML separately or all of them in a ZIP.

yaml-to-json.title: YAML to JSON
yaml-to-json.description: Convert YAML (including multiple documents and anchors) into valid JSON. Your files are never uploaded.
yaml-to-json.about: YAML to JSON reads YAML 1.2 files, including ones with several documents separated by ---, anchors and aliases, and merge keys (<<) like those in docker-compose or GitLab CI, and produces indented JSON. Several documents become a list. Custom tags are never executed: they are read as text.

faq.q1: Is it safe to open an unknown YAML file?
faq.a1: Yes. No code runs, and files with too many aliases, which can multiply their size until the device freezes (the billion laughs attack), are rejected with a warning.
faq.q2: Why doesn't yes become true?
faq.a2: Because in YAML 1.2, the current standard, only true and false are booleans. Likewise, dates stay as text in the JSON.
faq.q3: What if there are repeated keys or a syntax error?
faq.a3: You will see a warning instead of an incomplete JSON: a repeated key in the same object is an error in YAML.

json-to-toml.title: JSON to TOML
json-to-toml.description: Convert JSON into TOML for config files like pyproject.toml or Cargo.toml. In your browser.
json-to-toml.about: JSON to TOML turns a JSON object into a TOML file with tables ([section]) and arrays of tables ([[items]]), the config format of tools like Cargo, Poetry, Hugo or pyproject.toml. Keys with spaces or symbols are quoted.

faq.q1: Which JSON can be converted?
faq.a1: An object at the root. TOML doesn't allow a list or a bare value as a document: in that case you will see a warning explaining it.
faq.q2: What happens to null values?
faq.a2: TOML has no null: keys set to null are left out. A null inside a list can't be represented and you will see a warning.
faq.q3: Is any information lost?
faq.a3: Apart from nulls, no: strings, numbers, booleans, lists and nested objects are kept, and the TOML reads back the same.

toml-to-json.title: TOML to JSON
toml-to-json.description: Convert TOML files (Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, config.toml) into JSON. Your files are never uploaded.
toml-to-json.about: TOML to JSON reads TOML 1.0 files with tables, inline tables, arrays of tables and dates, and produces indented JSON. Use it to process a project's configuration with tools that only understand JSON, or to review its structure.

faq.q1: How are dates converted?
faq.a1: As ISO 8601 text: a date-time becomes 1979-05-27T07:32:00.000Z and a plain date 1979-05-27.
faq.q2: What about very large integers?
faq.a2: JSON in the browser can't hold integers above 2^53 without losing precision, so such a file is rejected with a warning instead of changing the value.
faq.q3: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a3: No. The conversion runs in your browser and the file never leaves your device.

json-to-xml.title: JSON to XML
json-to-xml.description: Convert JSON into a valid, indented XML document, attributes included. In your browser.
json-to-xml.about: JSON to XML builds a well-formed XML document from your JSON data. Keys starting with @ are written as attributes and #text as the element's text; lists become repeated elements. If the JSON has a single key at the root, that key is the root element; otherwise everything goes inside '<root>'.

faq.q1: What about keys that aren't valid XML names?
faq.a1: They are fixed so the XML stays valid: spaces and symbols become underscores (my key → my_key) and a name starting with a digit gets a leading underscore.
faq.q2: How do I write attributes?
faq.a2: Use keys starting with @: '{"book": {"@id": "1", "title": "Dune"}}' produces '<book id="1"><title>Dune</title></book>'.
faq.q3: Are special characters escaped?
faq.a3: Yes. &, '< and >' in text and quotes in attributes are written as entities, so the result is always valid XML.

xml-to-json.title: XML to JSON
xml-to-json.description: Convert XML into JSON with attributes, repeated elements and CDATA. Safe against XXE, and your files are never uploaded.
xml-to-json.about: XML to JSON reads XML documents and turns them into JSON: each element is a key, attributes get a leading @, repeated elements form a list and CDATA content is kept as text. Values stay text, because XML has no types: 007 stays 007.

faq.q1: Is it safe to open an unknown XML file?
faq.a1: Yes. Documents that declare entities ('<!ENTITY>'), the way in for attacks like XXE or billion laughs, are refused with a warning before reading, and nothing is fetched from the internet.
faq.q2: Why are numbers quoted?
faq.a2: Because in XML everything is text, and guessing types could change data (leading zeros, codes). This way you get exactly what the file says.
faq.q3: Are comments kept?
faq.a3: No. Comments and processing instructions have no JSON equivalent and are left out; the rest of the content is kept.

json-formatter.title: JSON formatter and validator
json-formatter.description: Validate your JSON, see the line and column of the error, and pretty-print or minify it.
json-formatter.about: The JSON formatter checks that your JSON is valid and, if it is, rewrites it indented with 2 or 4 spaces or tabs, or minifies it into a single line to save space. If there is an error, it tells you the line and column, for example an extra comma before a closing brace. It can also sort keys alphabetically to compare files.

faq.q1: How do I find the error in my JSON?
faq.a1: When formatting, the warning shows the line and column of the first problem. The most common ones are trailing commas, single quotes instead of double quotes and unquoted keys.
faq.q2: Does minifying change the data?
faq.a2: No. It only removes spaces and line breaks; values, order and types stay the same.
faq.q3: What is sorting keys for?
faq.a3: To compare two files with the same keys in a different order, or to get cleaner diffs in version control. Lists keep their order.

xml-formatter.title: XML formatter and validator
xml-formatter.description: Validate your XML, see the line and column of the error, and pretty-print or minify it.
xml-formatter.about: The XML formatter checks that the document is well-formed (closed tags, quoted attributes) and rewrites it indented or minified. Comments, CDATA sections, attributes and references like & are kept as they were. If there is an error, it shows the line and column.

faq.q1: Which errors does it find?
faq.a1: Unclosed or badly nested tags, repeated or unquoted attributes, and characters that aren't allowed. It is a well-formedness check: it does not validate against an XSD or DTD schema.
faq.q2: Is anything lost when formatting?
faq.a2: Whitespace between tags is replaced by the new indentation, and the DOCTYPE declaration is left out. Content, comments and CDATA are kept.
faq.q3: Is it safe with unknown files?
faq.a3: Yes. Documents that declare entities (the way in for XXE attacks) are refused with a warning, and nothing is fetched from the internet.

yaml-formatter.title: YAML formatter and validator
yaml-formatter.description: Validate your YAML, see the line and column of the error, and re-indent it keeping comments.
yaml-formatter.about: The YAML formatter validates config files such as docker-compose, Kubernetes or CI pipelines and re-indents them evenly with 2 or 4 spaces. It keeps comments, anchors and every document separated by ---. If there is a syntax error or a repeated key, it shows the line and column.

faq.q1: Why is there no tab option?
faq.a1: Because YAML doesn't allow tabs for indentation: a file indented with tabs is not valid.
faq.q2: Are my comments kept?
faq.a2: Yes. Full-line and end-of-line comments are kept, as are anchors and aliases.
faq.q3: Does it catch repeated keys?
faq.a3: Yes. A repeated key at the same level is an error in YAML, and many programs silently take the last one; here you get a warning with its position.

base64-encode.title: Base64 encode
base64-encode.description: Turn text or any file into Base64 or a data URL to embed it in HTML, CSS or JSON.
base64-encode.about: Base64 encode turns text (as UTF-8) or the bytes of any file (image, PDF, font) into Base64 text, the format used to embed files in HTML, CSS, JSON or email. Get plain Base64, wrapped every 76 characters as email expects, or a data URL ready for a src attribute.

faq.q1: How big is the result?
faq.a1: Base64 is about 33% larger than the original file: every 3 bytes are written as 4 characters.
faq.q2: Does Base64 encrypt my data?
faq.a2: No. It is an encoding, not encryption: anyone can decode it. Don't use it to protect passwords or private information.
faq.q3: What is a data URL?
faq.a3: It is the Base64 preceded by the file type, like data:image/png;base64,…, and it can be used directly as an image src or in CSS.

base64-decode.title: Base64 decode
base64-decode.description: Turn Base64 or a data URL back into the original text or file, with its type detected.
base64-decode.about: Base64 decode recovers the original bytes from Base64 text or a data URL and gives you the file to download. It detects the type from the data URL or the content (PNG, JPG, PDF and more) and picks the extension; if the result is text, it is shown so you can copy it. Line breaks, the URL-safe alphabet (- and _) and missing = padding are accepted.

faq.q1: How do I know which file was inside?
faq.a1: If the Base64 comes in a data URL, its declared type is used; otherwise it is recognized from the content. If it can't be recognized, it downloads as .bin with the exact bytes.
faq.q2: Why does it say it isn't valid Base64?
faq.a2: Because it contains characters outside the Base64 alphabet or a piece is missing. Check that you copied all of it.
faq.q3: Is the decoded file identical to the original?
faq.a3: Yes, byte for byte. Decoding doesn't recompress or change anything.

url-encode.title: URL encode and decode
url-encode.description: Encode text for use in a URL (%20, %C3%B1) or decode a URL back into readable text.
url-encode.about: URL encode turns spaces, accents and symbols into percent sequences (for example ñ becomes %C3%B1) so they can be used safely in links and parameters. Encode a value, which also escapes / ? & and =, or a whole URL, which keeps them. Decode mode does the opposite and can read + as a space, as in web forms.

faq.q1: What's the difference between a value and a whole URL?
faq.a1: For a parameter, such as search text, & = ? and / must be escaped so they don't break the URL. In a whole URL those characters have a role and are kept as they are.
faq.q2: Why does + become a space?
faq.a2: Web forms send spaces as +. Uncheck the option if + means a plus sign in your text.
faq.q3: What about a malformed %?
faq.a3: You will see a warning: a sequence like %E0%A4%A is incomplete and doesn't stand for any character.

hash-generator.title: MD5 and SHA hash generator
hash-generator.description: Calculate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 of text or files and verify a checksum.
hash-generator.about: The hash generator calculates MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 checksums of text (as UTF-8) or of any file without uploading it: files are read in parts in your browser, so large files work too. Paste the hash published by whoever distributes a file to check that your download is complete and has not been altered. The result downloads as checksums.txt in the format sha256sum -c reads.

faq.q1: How do I check that a download is not damaged?
faq.a1: Choose the file, paste the checksum from the official site into “Expected hash” and calculate. You will see whether it matches and with which algorithm; it is recognized by its length.
faq.q2: Which algorithm should I use?
faq.a2: SHA-256 or SHA-512. MD5 and SHA-1 catch download errors, but they are no longer safe against someone deliberately crafting files with the same hash.
faq.q3: Can a hash be used to store passwords?
faq.a3: Not directly: passwords need slow, salted functions such as bcrypt or Argon2. Fast hashes like these are for verifying files and integrity.

uuid-generator.title: UUID generator
uuid-generator.description: Generate random v4 or time-ordered v7 UUIDs, one or in bulk, with or without hyphens.
uuid-generator.about: The UUID generator creates unique identifiers following RFC 9562 with your browser's cryptographic random generator. Version 4 is fully random; version 7 starts with the date and time in milliseconds, so the identifiers sort by creation time, which is handy as a primary key in databases. You can generate up to 10,000 at once, in upper case or without hyphens, and download them as text.

faq.q1: Can two UUIDs be the same?
faq.a1: Not in practice: a v4 UUID has 122 random bits, so the chance of a repeat is negligible even after billions of them.
faq.q2: When should I use version 7?
faq.a2: When the identifiers are database keys: since they are ordered by time, indexes fragment less than with v4 UUIDs. Keep in mind that they reveal when they were created.
faq.q3: Are the generated UUIDs stored?
faq.a3: No. They are generated in your browser and never sent to a server.

timestamp-converter.title: Unix timestamp converter
timestamp-converter.description: Convert Unix timestamps in seconds or milliseconds to date and time in any time zone, and dates to timestamps.
timestamp-converter.about: The timestamp converter turns Unix timestamps (seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds) into readable dates and dates into timestamps. Paste one per line: it detects the unit from the number of digits and also accepts ISO 8601 dates (2023-11-14T22:13:20Z) or email-style dates (RFC 2822). For each line you get the seconds, the milliseconds, the date in UTC and the time in the time zone you choose, with its UTC offset and daylight saving time applied.

faq.q1: How does it know whether a number is in seconds or milliseconds?
faq.a1: From the number of digits: up to 11 is seconds, up to 14 milliseconds, up to 17 microseconds and more is nanoseconds. If your data differs, choose the unit yourself.
faq.q2: Which zone is used for a date without a time zone?
faq.a2: The zone chosen in the selector. If the date includes Z or an offset such as -03:00, that one is used.
faq.q3: What about daylight saving time?
faq.a3: It is applied with your browser's time zone database. If a local time happens twice when clocks go back, the first one is used.

qr-generator.title: QR code generator
qr-generator.description: Create QR codes for text, links, Wi-Fi networks or contacts and download them as PNG or SVG.
qr-generator.about: The QR code generator turns text, a link, Wi-Fi network details or a contact card (vCard) into a code any phone reads with its camera. Choose the size, the error correction level and the colors, then download it as PNG to use right away or as SVG to print at any size without losing sharpness. The code never expires and doesn't go through a link shortener: it holds your data directly.

faq.q1: Does the QR code stop working over time?
faq.a1: No. The data is inside the code itself, with no redirects or services in between, so it works as long as the image can be read.
faq.q2: Which error correction level should I choose?
faq.a2: Medium works for almost everything. Use a higher level if the code is printed on surfaces that can get scratched or stained; it uses more modules, so the code looks denser.
faq.q3: How do I share my Wi-Fi with a QR code?
faq.a3: Choose Wi-Fi and enter the network name and password with the same security type your router uses. When scanned, Android and iPhone offer to join without typing the password.

qr-reader.title: Read a QR code from an image
qr-reader.description: Read the content of a QR code in a photo or screenshot, without using the camera.
qr-reader.about: The QR code reader finds the code in a photo or screenshot (PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF, BMP or AVIF) and shows its content so you can copy it: a link, text, Wi-Fi details or a contact. It also reads light codes on dark backgrounds and tries several scales to find small codes in large photos. The image is analyzed in your browser.

faq.q1: Why can't it find the code in my photo?
faq.a1: Usually the photo is blurry, taken at a steep angle, or the code is cut off. Crop the image around the code or take the photo straight on in good light.
faq.q2: Does it open the link automatically?
faq.a2: No. It only shows the content, so you can check where a link goes before opening it.
faq.q3: Can it read several codes at once?
faq.a3: You can choose several images and get the content of each; one code is read from each image.

password-generator.title: Password generator
password-generator.description: Create strong random passwords with the length and characters you choose.
password-generator.about: The password generator creates random passwords with your browser's cryptographic random generator, without bias: every character is equally likely. Choose the length, whether to use upper case, lower case, numbers and symbols, and whether to avoid look-alike characters such as l, 1, O and 0. Every password includes at least one character of each chosen type, and you'll see its strength in bits of entropy.

faq.q1: How long should a password be?
faq.a1: At least 16 characters with letters, numbers and symbols (about 100 bits). For the master password of a password manager, 20 or more is better.
faq.q2: Do you store or see the passwords I generate?
faq.a2: No. They are generated in your browser and never sent to a server. Close the tab when you're done.
faq.q3: What do bits of entropy mean?
faq.a3: They measure how many guesses it would take: each bit doubles the number. From 80 bits on, a random password withstands brute-force attacks even offline.

word-counter.title: Word and character counter
word-counter.description: Count words, characters, sentences and paragraphs as you type, and switch text to upper or lower case.
word-counter.about: The word counter instantly shows how many words, characters (with and without spaces), sentences, paragraphs and lines your text has, plus an estimated reading time. It counts characters as they appear, so an emoji or an accented letter counts as one, and it finds words in Chinese too, which has no spaces. You can also switch the text to UPPER CASE, lower case, Title Case or Sentence case, copy it or download it.

faq.q1: Does it count like Word or Google Docs?
faq.a1: Almost always. Hyphenated words or numbers with commas may differ, because each program applies its own rules; this one uses the Unicode rules for the page's language.
faq.q2: Can I count a file?
faq.a2: Yes: open a text file (.txt, .md, .csv, .srt…) and it loads into the box. If it comes from Windows with accents in another encoding, that is detected automatically.
faq.q3: How is the reading time calculated?
faq.a3: At 200 words per minute, rounded up.

color-converter.title: Color converter
color-converter.description: Convert colors between HEX, RGB, HSL and OKLCH and check accessibility contrast (WCAG).
color-converter.about: The color converter reads a color in HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH or by its CSS name and shows it in all of those formats, ready to copy into your CSS or design tool. It also calculates the color's contrast on a background following the WCAG 2 guidelines and tells you whether it meets AA and AAA for normal and large text, so your text stays readable.

faq.q1: What is OKLCH for?
faq.a1: It describes colors by lightness, chroma and hue in a way that matches how we perceive them. It makes harmonious palettes easier, and every modern browser accepts it in CSS.
faq.q2: How much contrast does text need?
faq.a2: Level AA asks for at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; level AAA, 7:1 and 4.5:1.
faq.q3: Does it accept transparent colors?
faq.a3: Yes: #RRGGBBAA, rgb(… / 0.5) and similar. For contrast, the color is blended with the background the way a browser would.

unit-converter.title: Unit converter
unit-converter.description: Convert length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, data and time between metric and imperial units.
unit-converter.about: The unit converter instantly converts a value between metric, imperial and US units: length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, data size and time. It uses exact definitions (1 inch = 2.54 cm, 1 pound = 453.59237 g) and shows the value in every unit at once. Both decimal points and decimal commas are accepted.

faq.q1: Are cups and gallons US or UK measures?
faq.a1: Teaspoons, tablespoons, cups, pints, quarts and gallons are US customary measures; the British imperial gallon is listed separately.
faq.q2: Why isn't a GB 1024 MB?
faq.a2: With SI prefixes, 1 GB = 1000 MB. Operating systems sometimes count in powers of 2: those are GiB and MiB, which you can convert too.
faq.q3: How precise are the results?
faq.a3: Up to 10 significant digits are shown. The equivalences are exact by definition; the number is only rounded for display.

compress-image.title: Compress image
compress-image.description: Shrink JPG, PNG, WEBP and AVIF photos, or fit them under an exact file size for a form.
compress-image.about: Compress image re-encodes your photos so they take less space without changing their pixel size. Pick a level (low, recommended or strong) or an exact maximum size, like the 100 KB or 200 KB many online forms ask for: we find the best quality that fits and, if that is not enough, scale the image down. PNG files are optimized losslessly at the low level and reduced to a color palette at the others. You can also switch to WEBP or AVIF, which are smaller at the same quality. Everything happens in your browser, and metadata (such as GPS location) is removed.

faq.q1: How much smaller will my photo get?
faq.a1: It depends on the photo: a phone JPG usually drops 40% to 80% at the recommended level. If the image was already optimized and can't get smaller, you get the original back unchanged.
faq.q2: How do I get a photo under 100 KB for a form?
faq.a2: Choose “Exact file size” and the 100 KB button (or type another size). The result is at most that size; if needed its pixel size is reduced too, and we tell you by how much.
faq.q3: Why was my PNG saved as JPG?
faq.a3: In exact-size mode PNG files are saved as JPG, because PNG has no quality setting. If your PNG has transparency, choose WEBP to keep it.
faq.a4: With JPG, WEBP and AVIF, a little: the low level is barely noticeable and the strong level favors size. PNG at the low level loses nothing.

resize-image.title: Resize image
resize-image.description: Change the size of your images in pixels, by percentage or to each social network's dimensions.
resize-image.about: Resize image changes the width and height of your photos: type the pixels you want (keeping the proportions or not), a percentage, or pick a ready-made social media size such as an Instagram square post, a story or a YouTube thumbnail. When the proportions don't match, you can crop the edges or add borders so nothing of the photo is lost. It works with JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF and HEIC, in batches, and you can change the format at the same time. Everything is processed in your browser.

faq.q1: Is an image smaller than the requested size enlarged?
faq.a1: In pixel mode with proportions, no, unless you tick “Allow enlarging smaller images”, since enlarging adds no detail. Social media sizes do enlarge it to fill the format.
faq.q2: What if the photo doesn't have the social network's proportions?
faq.a2: “Crop the edges” keeps the center of the photo and crops what doesn't fit. “Add borders” fits the whole photo and fills the sides (white for JPG, transparent for PNG, WEBP and AVIF).
faq.q3: Is there a maximum size?
faq.a3: The result can have up to about 36 megapixels (for example 6928 × 5196); larger requests are scaled down keeping the shape. Each file can be up to 50 MB.
faq.q4: Does it work with animated GIFs?
faq.a4: Only the first frame is resized. A video-to-GIF tool for animated GIFs will come later.

rotate-image.title: Rotate image
rotate-image.description: Turn your photos 90° or 180° and mirror them, in batches.
rotate-image.about: Rotate image turns your photos 90° right, 90° left or 180°, and can also mirror them (horizontal flip) or turn them upside down (vertical flip). The orientation saved by the camera is applied first, so the result is exactly what you see on screen and looks the same in every app. It works with JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF and HEIC, in batches, and keeps the format (HEIC is saved as JPG). Everything is processed in your browser.

faq.q1: My photo looks fine on my phone but sideways on my computer. Does this help?
faq.a1: Yes. Choose “Just straighten”: the orientation saved by the camera is applied and the photo stays upright in every app, without turning it further.
faq.q2: Do I lose quality when rotating?
faq.a2: PNG, BMP, TIFF and GIF lose nothing. JPG, WEBP and AVIF are saved again at high quality (92), a difference you won't notice in practice.
faq.q3: Can I rotate and flip at the same time?
faq.a3: Yes: the image is rotated first and flipped after. For example, 90° right with a horizontal flip.
faq.a4: No: saving the rotated image removes the metadata, including GPS location. To remove metadata without touching the image, use “Remove EXIF metadata”.

remove-exif.title: Remove EXIF metadata
remove-exif.description: Erase GPS location, camera and date from your photos without losing quality.
remove-exif.about: Remove EXIF metadata erases the information you can't see but that travels with the file: the GPS location where the photo was taken, the camera or phone make and model, the date and time, the software used and the author. Before erasing, we show you what each photo contained. For JPG, PNG and WEBP the image is not compressed again: the same image data is copied without the metadata, so quality is identical. JPGs keep only their orientation, so the photo doesn't show sideways, and their color profile. HEIC files are saved as JPG without metadata. Everything happens in your browser.

faq.q1: Why remove metadata before sharing a photo?
faq.a1: A phone photo can carry the exact coordinates of your home or workplace. Many social networks remove them, but email, chat attachments and cloud links usually send the original file.
faq.q2: Does the photo lose quality?
faq.a2: Not for JPG, PNG or WEBP: the image data is copied byte for byte. Only HEIC files are saved again, as high-quality JPG.
faq.q3: What is kept?
faq.a3: What's needed to display the photo correctly: the orientation (JPG) and the color profile. GPS, camera, dates, software, author, thumbnails, XMP, IPTC and comments are removed.
faq.q4: How do I check the location is gone?
faq.a4: Run the clean photo through this tool again: it should say it found no metadata. You can also check the file's properties on your computer.

crop-image.title: Crop image
crop-image.description: Crop your photos freely or to a fixed aspect ratio (1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16…), pixel-exact and without uploading them anywhere.
crop-image.about: Crop image lets you pick the part of the photo you want to keep: drag the box and its corners, or type the exact position and size in pixels. You can lock an aspect ratio (square 1:1 for profile pictures, 4:5 for Instagram, 16:9 for covers and videos, 9:16 for stories, the original ratio…) or crop freely. It also works with the keyboard alone. It accepts JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF and HEIC, and you can change the format when saving. Everything runs in your browser.

faq.q1: Does cropping lose quality?
faq.a1: The pixels in the chosen area are copied as they are, with no scaling. PNG, BMP, TIFF and GIF lose nothing; JPG, WEBP and AVIF are saved again at high quality (92).
faq.q2: How do I crop with the keyboard only?
faq.a2: Tab to the crop box: the arrow keys move it and Shift + arrows resize it (1% of the image per press). For exact values, type X, Y, width and height in pixels and press Enter.
faq.q3: Can I crop several photos at once?
faq.a3: No: the crop is set on each photo, so it's one at a time. To bring many photos to the same size, use “Resize image” with a social media size and the crop-edges option.
faq.q4: Why is the preview smaller than my photo?
faq.a4: A reduced copy is shown so editing stays fast, but the crop is applied to the full original image: the pixel values are those of the real photo.

watermark-image.title: Watermark images
watermark-image.description: Add your name, text or logo as a watermark to many photos at once, in a corner or tiled.
watermark-image.about: Watermark images protects your photos with a text (your name, your brand, “sample”, “confidential”) or with your logo. Pick the position on a 9-spot grid or a tilted tile pattern that covers the whole image, the size, color and opacity, and check the result in the preview before processing. It is applied the same way to every photo in the batch, sized in proportion to each one. It works with JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF and HEIC, and everything runs in your browser.

faq.q1: Can I use my logo with a transparent background?
faq.a1: Yes: choose “Logo or image” and upload a PNG or WEBP with transparency. The logo is scaled to a percentage of each photo's width, so it looks the same on large and small photos.
faq.q2: What is the tiled option for?
faq.a2: It repeats the watermark, tilted, over the whole image. It is harder to crop out or erase than a corner mark, so it suits documents or photos you share as samples.
faq.q3: Can the watermark be removed later?
faq.a3: Not from the new file: the mark is drawn into the pixels. Keep your originals without the mark; the tool never changes them.
faq.a4: PNG, BMP, TIFF and GIF lose nothing. JPG, WEBP and AVIF are saved again at high quality (92). The size in pixels doesn't change.

add-text-to-image.title: Add text to image
add-text-to-image.description: Write on your photos with the font, size, color, outline and position you choose, with an instant preview.
add-text-to-image.about: Add text to image lets you write one or more lines over a photo: a title, a date, a price, a quote to share. Choose the font, bold, size, color, an outline that reads on any background or a box behind the text, and the position on a 9-spot grid. The preview updates as you type. You can apply the same text to several images. It works with JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF and HEIC, in your browser.

faq.q1: Can I write several lines?
faq.a1: Yes: each line break in the text box starts a new line, centered on each other. You can write up to 500 characters.
faq.q2: Which fonts are available?
faq.a2: Sans serif, serif and monospace, using your system's fonts; accents, emoji and Chinese show as they do on your device.
faq.q3: The text is hard to read on my photo. What can I do?
faq.a3: Turn on “Outline”, which adds a border of the opposite color around each letter, or “Box behind the text”, which adds a translucent box.
faq.q4: Does the text size depend on the photo?
faq.a4: Yes: it is a percentage of the image's shorter side, so the text looks equally big on a phone photo and on a small screenshot.

favicon-generator.title: Favicon generator
favicon-generator.description: Create your website's favicon from an image or an SVG: ICO, PNGs for Apple and Android, manifest and HTML tags.
favicon-generator.about: The favicon generator turns your logo into every icon a website needs: favicon.ico with 16, 32 and 48 pixels for tabs and bookmarks, 16 and 32 px PNGs, the 180 px icon for the iPhone home screen (apple-touch-icon), the 192 and 512 px icons for Android, the site.webmanifest file and an HTML snippet ready to paste into your head. It accepts PNG, JPG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC and SVG; if the image isn't square, you can fit it with margins or crop it. Everything is generated in your browser.

faq.q1: Where do I put the files?
faq.a1: At the root of your site (next to the home page), and paste the contents of favicon-head.html inside the head of your pages. If you use another folder, change the paths that start with “/”.
faq.q2: Why does the Apple icon have a background?
faq.a2: iPhones paint transparent areas of home-screen icons black, so apple-touch-icon.png is saved with the chosen background (or white). The others keep transparency if you chose a transparent background.
faq.q3: Which image works best?
faq.a3: An SVG or a square PNG of at least 512 × 512 px with a simple, high-contrast design: at 16 px fine details and long text can't be made out.
faq.a4: The SVG is drawn in your browser as an image, without running scripts or loading external resources, and it is never sent to any server.

svg-converter.title: Convert SVG to PNG, JPG or WEBP
svg-converter.description: Turn your SVG graphics into high-resolution PNG, JPG or WEBP images (2×, 4× or any width), in batches.
svg-converter.about: Convert SVG turns vector logos, icons and illustrations into images you can use anywhere: social media, documents, slides or sites that don't accept SVG. Since an SVG is vector-based, it is drawn directly at the requested size and stays sharp when enlarged: choose 1×, 2×, 4× or an exact width in pixels. PNG and WEBP keep transparency; JPG fills it with white. You can convert many files at once and everything happens in your browser.

faq.q1: Does it get pixelated if I enlarge it?
faq.a1: No: the SVG is drawn again at the final size, so at 2× or 4× lines and text stay sharp. The limit is 16,384 px per side.
faq.q2: Is it safe to convert an SVG I didn't make?
faq.a2: Yes. The SVG is drawn as an image: any scripts it contains don't run and external files are not loaded. It is also never uploaded to any server.
faq.q3: My SVG uses a special font and the text looks different. Why?
faq.a3: If the SVG uses a font that isn't embedded in the file, the browser replaces it with a system font. Convert text to outlines in your editor (Inkscape, Illustrator, Figma) before exporting.
faq.q4: What size is the result at 1×?
faq.a4: The one the SVG declares in its width and height attributes (or its viewBox). If it declares none, 1024 px is used. The result message shows each image's final size.

subtitle-converter.title: Convert SRT, VTT, ASS and SSA subtitles
subtitle-converter.description: Convert subtitles between SRT, WebVTT, ASS and SSA keeping timings, italics and bold, in batches and without uploading your files.
subtitle-converter.about: Subtitle converter moves your files between SRT (the most compatible one: media players, TVs and YouTube), WebVTT (used by HTML5 video on web pages), ASS and SSA (Aegisub formats with styles). Timings stay exact, as do line breaks, italics, bold and underline. The text encoding is detected: an old SRT saved as Windows-1252 is read with its accents, and the result is always saved as UTF-8. Convert several files at once or paste the text.

faq.q1: Is anything lost when converting ASS to SRT?
faq.a1: SRT and VTT have no fonts, colors or positions like ASS does. Text, timings, italics, bold and underline are kept; the rest is removed, and a note below the result tells you when that happens.
faq.q2: My subtitles show odd symbols instead of accented letters. Can this fix it?
faq.a2: Usually, yes. When a file is not valid UTF-8 it is read as Windows-1252 (common in older European and Latin American files) and the result is saved as UTF-8, which every modern player understands.
faq.q3: What happens to comments and styles in a VTT file?
faq.a3: NOTE blocks are skipped because they are not subtitles. STYLE blocks, per-cue positions and speaker names are removed when converting to another format.
faq.q4: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: No. The conversion runs in your browser; your subtitles never leave your device.

subtitle-sync.title: Sync subtitles (shift timing and change FPS)
subtitle-sync.description: Shift every subtitle in an SRT, VTT, ASS or SSA file earlier or later, and fix drift between 23.976, 24, 25 and 30 FPS.
subtitle-sync.about: Subtitle sync fixes files that show up before or after the words are spoken. Type how many seconds to move them (a negative number makes them earlier) and, if the gap keeps growing during the film, change the frame rate: the classic case is a subtitle made for 23.976 FPS on a 25 FPS video. Only the timings change: the file's format, styles, positions and comments stay untouched. No timing ends up before the start of the video.

faq.q1: How do I know how many seconds to shift?
faq.a1: Find a clear line in the video, note the second it is spoken and compare it with that line's time in the subtitle file. If the subtitle shows up 2 seconds late, type -2; if it shows up early, a positive number.
faq.q2: It matches at the start but drifts by the end. What should I do?
faq.a2: That is a frame rate problem: the subtitle was made for another release of the video. Turn on "Change the frame rate" and choose the source and target rates; the most common pairs are 23.976 ↔ 25.
faq.q3: What happens to lines that would land before the start?
faq.a3: Lines ending before second zero are removed (we tell you how many) and lines crossing it start at zero. SRT cues are renumbered.
faq.q4: Will my ASS file lose its styles?
faq.a4: No. Only each line's start and end times are rewritten; styles, positions, effects and comments stay as they were.

font-converter.title: Convert fonts: TTF, OTF, WOFF and WOFF2
font-converter.description: Convert TTF or OTF fonts to WOFF2 or WOFF for your website, or turn WOFF/WOFF2 back into TTF/OTF to install. Free, in your browser.
font-converter.about: The font converter gets typefaces ready for the web and the desktop. WOFF2 compresses the font with Brotli and is usually 30% smaller than WOFF and half the original TTF, so your site loads faster; WOFF covers very old browsers. The other way round, if you only have a WOFF or WOFF2, you get the TTF or OTF to install on Windows, macOS or Linux. Glyphs, metrics and names don’t change: only the wrapper does.

faq.q1: Is quality lost?
faq.a1: No. WOFF and WOFF2 are compressed forms of the same font: back to TTF or OTF you get the same glyphs, metrics, kerning and names.
faq.q2: Can I convert OTF to TTF?
faq.a2: No: this tool doesn’t change the outline type (CFF ↔ TrueType), only the container. An OTF (CFF) font comes out as .otf; desktop apps install it just like a TTF.
faq.q3: Can I use any font on my website?
faq.a3: It depends on its license. Many commercial fonts forbid converting them or using them on the web; Google Fonts and other OFL-licensed fonts allow it. Check the license before publishing.
faq.a4: No. Conversion happens in your browser and the files never leave your device.

markdown-to-html.title: Markdown to HTML
markdown-to-html.description: Convert Markdown (with GitHub tables and task lists) to clean, safe HTML, as a fragment or a full page. In your browser.
markdown-to-html.about: Markdown to HTML turns notes, READMEs or docs written in Markdown into HTML ready to paste into a website, an email or a CMS. It supports the GitHub flavor: tables, strikethrough, task lists and fenced code blocks with a language. Get just the content or a complete page with a title and readable light and dark styles.

faq.q1: Which Markdown flavor is supported?
faq.a1: CommonMark with the GitHub extensions (GFM): tables, ~~strikethrough~~, task lists, autolinks and fenced code blocks with a language.
faq.q2: Is the generated HTML safe?
faq.a2: Yes. It’s cleaned with DOMPurify: no scripts, event attributes (onclick, onerror), forms or javascript: links remain. HTML written inside the Markdown is kept only if it’s safe.
faq.q3: Can I convert several files?
faq.a3: Yes. Pick several .md files and download them in a ZIP, or paste the text directly.
faq.a4: No. The conversion happens in your browser.

html-to-markdown.title: HTML to Markdown
html-to-markdown.description: Convert HTML pages or snippets to clean Markdown (with GitHub tables) for docs, wikis or notes. In your browser.
html-to-markdown.about: HTML to Markdown turns the content of a web page, an email or a CMS export into easy-to-edit Markdown: # headings, lists, bold, links, images, tables and fenced code blocks with a language. Scripts, styles and forms are dropped. Great for moving content to GitHub, Notion, Obsidian or a static site generator.

faq.q1: Does anything in the HTML run?
faq.a1: No. The HTML is parsed as inert text: scripts don’t run and no images or external resources are loaded.
faq.q2: What happens to styles, colors and layout?
faq.a2: Markdown has no styles: the structure (headings, lists, tables, emphasis) is kept and colors, fonts and positions are lost.
faq.q3: Are tables kept?
faq.a3: Yes, as GitHub Markdown tables. Merged cells don’t exist in Markdown and are simplified.
faq.a4: No. Everything happens in your browser.

delete-pdf-pages.title: Delete pages from a PDF
delete-pdf-pages.description: Remove unwanted pages from a PDF by picking them on thumbnails or by number, without uploading the file.
delete-pdf-pages.about: Delete PDF pages lets you remove blank sheets, appendices or duplicate pages before sending a document. You see a thumbnail of every page: tap the ones you don't need (they turn red) or type their numbers, such as 2, 5-7. The rest of the document stays the same, in the same order and quality, because pages are copied without being recompressed.

faq.q1: Does deleting pages reduce quality?
faq.a1: No. The remaining pages are copied as they are, with selectable text, images and internal page links.
faq.q2: Can I pick pages by typing their numbers?
faq.a2: Yes. Type comma-separated ranges such as 1-3, 8 or 10- (page 10 to the end). Thumbnails are marked automatically, and tapping a thumbnail updates the field.
faq.q3: Why can't I delete every page?
faq.a3: A PDF with no pages is not valid and most apps won't open it. Keep at least one page.
faq.a4: No. Thumbnails and the new PDF are made in your browser; the file never leaves your device.

extract-pdf-pages.title: Extract pages from a PDF
extract-pdf-pages.description: Pick pages on thumbnails and save them as a new PDF, or each one as its own PDF.
extract-pdf-pages.about: Extract PDF pages creates a new document with only the pages you choose: a certificate from a long file, a chapter of a book or the sheets that need signing. Tap the thumbnails (they get a check mark) or type the numbers, then choose one PDF or one PDF per page in a ZIP. Pages keep the original order and are copied without losing quality.

faq.q1: In what order are the extracted pages?
faq.a1: In the same order as in the original document. If you need another order, use Organize PDF afterwards.
faq.q2: How is this different from Split PDF?
faq.a2: Split PDF cuts the whole document into ranges. Here you visually pick only the pages you care about, one by one.
faq.q3: Can I get every page as a separate file?
faq.a3: Yes. Choose "One PDF per page (ZIP)" to download a ZIP with one PDF for each selected page, named with its page number.
faq.a4: No. A new file is created in your browser and the original stays the same on your device.

pdf-page-numbers.title: Add page numbers to a PDF
pdf-page-numbers.description: Add page numbers to your PDFs in the position and format you choose, rotated pages included.
pdf-page-numbers.about: Add page numbers puts a number on every sheet of a thesis, contract or case file. Choose a corner or the center, top or bottom, the format (1, "1 / 10" or "Page 1 of 10"), the size and the first number; you can leave the cover unnumbered. Numbers are written as real text and stay upright even when a page is stored sideways. Number several PDFs at once.

faq.q1: Can I leave the cover without a number?
faq.a1: Yes. Tick "No number on the first page": numbering starts on the second sheet with the number you choose (for example 1).
faq.q2: What about landscape or rotated pages?
faq.a2: The number is placed according to how the page looks when opened: bottom center is bottom center on a landscape page or a scan stored sideways too.
faq.q3: Can I start at another number?
faq.a3: Yes. Type the first number, for example 15 if the PDF continues another document. The total in "Page N of M" adjusts by itself.
faq.a4: No. Numbers are added in your browser and your files never leave your device.

pdf-watermark.title: Add a watermark to a PDF
pdf-watermark.description: Stamp text such as CONFIDENTIAL or DRAFT on your PDFs, diagonally, horizontally or tiled, with the opacity you want.
pdf-watermark.about: Add a watermark to a PDF stamps text on the pages to mark a copy, a draft or a confidential document, or to identify who you sent it to. Choose the text, the layout (one large diagonal, a horizontal line across the center or a repeated pattern covering the whole sheet), the size, color and opacity, and whether it goes on every page or only some. Accented letters work, and so do Chinese characters and emoji.

faq.q1: Does the watermark hide the content?
faq.a1: It is drawn on top with the opacity you choose: at 20–30% the document's text stays easy to read.
faq.q2: Can it be removed later?
faq.a2: It is written into the pages as content, so it can't be removed with one click. Still, someone with a PDF editor could take it out: it doesn't replace a signature or password protection.
faq.q3: Can I mark only some pages?
faq.a3: Yes. Choose "Only some" and type pages or ranges, for example 1, 3-5. With several PDFs, the pages apply to each one.
faq.a4: No. The watermark is added in your browser and the file never leaves your device.

pdf-to-text.title: PDF to text
pdf-to-text.description: Extract the text of your PDFs into a TXT file to copy, search or reuse it, without uploading them.
pdf-to-text.about: PDF to text copies all the text in a PDF into a UTF-8 TXT file, page by page in reading order, so you can paste it into an email, search for a phrase or reuse a contract without retyping it. You can mark where each page starts and process several PDFs at once. If the PDF is a scan (images only), we tell you: that text needs optical character recognition (OCR).

faq.q1: Are formatting, tables or columns kept?
faq.a1: No. The result is plain text: words and line breaks are kept, but not fonts, colors or exact positions. Tables come out as lines of text.
faq.q2: Why does it say my PDF has no text?
faq.a2: Because it is a scanned image or a photo saved as PDF: it holds pixels, not letters. Getting that text out needs OCR.
faq.q3: Does it work with accents and other languages?
faq.a3: Yes. Text is saved as UTF-8, with accents and Chinese characters too, as long as the PDF holds them as text.
faq.a4: No. Text is extracted in your browser and your files never leave your device.

crop-pdf.title: Crop PDF margins
crop-pdf.description: Remove white margins from a PDF automatically or by millimeters, without losing quality.
crop-pdf.about: Crop PDF removes the margins you don't need: great for reading an article on a phone or e-reader, or for trimming a scanned document with borders. Automatic mode finds where each page's content ends and keeps 3 mm around it; manual mode removes the millimeters you choose from each side. Only the visible area (CropBox) changes, so text and images are not recompressed.

faq.q1: Is the cropped part deleted from the file?
faq.a1: No. It is hidden outside the visible area and viewers don't show or print it, but it is still inside the file. Don't use this tool to hide private data.
faq.q2: How does automatic mode work?
faq.a2: Each page is drawn at low resolution to find the content that isn't white, then cropped around it with a 3 mm margin. A blank page stays as it is.
faq.q3: Does it work with rotated or landscape pages?
faq.a3: Yes. Top, bottom, left and right follow how the page looks when you open it.
faq.a4: No. Everything happens in your browser and the file never leaves your device.

sign-pdf.title: Sign PDF
sign-pdf.description: Draw your signature or upload a photo and place it on any page of a PDF, without printing or scanning.
sign-pdf.about: Sign PDF lets you put your handwritten signature on a contract, an authorization or a form without printing or scanning it. Draw it with your finger or mouse, or upload a photo of your signature on paper (the white background is removed for you). Then pick the page, tap where it goes and adjust its size. The signature is saved as an image on the page, with transparency. It is a visible signature, not a digital signature with a certificate.

faq.q1: Is it legally valid?
faq.a1: It depends on the process and the country. It is equivalent to pasting a scanned signature: fine for many private agreements, but it is not a certified digital signature like one from a token or an official certificate. If a digital signature is required, this doesn't replace it.
faq.q2: Can I use a photo of my signature?
faq.a2: Yes. Sign on white paper, take a well-lit photo and upload it: we remove the white paper and trim the edges so only the stroke remains.
faq.q3: Can I move the signature with the keyboard?
faq.a3: Yes. Select the signature with Tab and move it with the arrow keys; hold Shift to move it faster.
faq.q4: Are my signature or my PDF uploaded?
faq.a4: No. Everything happens in your browser: neither the signature nor the document leaves your device, and we don't keep your signature.

protect-pdf.title: Password protect a PDF
protect-pdf.description: Add a password to your PDF with 256-bit AES encryption and choose whether it can be printed or copied. Free, in your browser.
protect-pdf.about: Protect PDF adds an open password to your documents: without it, no viewer can show the content. It uses 256-bit AES, the strongest encryption the PDF format supports, and you can choose whether people who open it may print it, copy its text or edit it. Handy for emailing receipts, contracts or medical records with more peace of mind.

faq.q1: How secure is it?
faq.a1: It uses 256-bit AES (PDF 2.0). Security depends on the password: use a long one with words or varied characters, and share it through a different channel than the email itself.
faq.q2: What if I forget the password?
faq.a2: It can’t be recovered: we don’t store it anywhere. Keep a copy of the original PDF without a password.
faq.q3: Do the print and copy permissions work?
faq.a3: Adobe Acrobat, browsers and most viewers respect them, but some programs ignore them. The open password, on the other hand, is always required.
faq.a4: No. Encryption happens in your browser with qpdf, and neither the file nor the password leaves your device.

unlock-pdf.title: Remove a PDF password
unlock-pdf.description: Remove the password from a PDF you can open: type it once and download a copy without a password or restrictions.
unlock-pdf.about: If you have a protected PDF (a bank statement, an invoice or a work document) and you’re tired of typing the password every time, type it here once and get an unencrypted copy. It also removes print or copy restrictions if you know the permissions password. It can’t open other people’s PDFs: the right password is required.

faq.q1: Can it find a password I don’t know?
faq.a1: No. The tool only removes the password if you type it correctly. We don’t try passwords or break the encryption.
faq.q2: Which password do I type?
faq.a2: The one you use to open the PDF. If the PDF opens without a password but won’t let you print or copy, type the permissions (owner) password.
faq.q3: Is anything in the document lost?
faq.a3: No. Only the encryption is removed; text, images, forms and links stay the same.
faq.q4: Are my PDF and password uploaded?
faq.a4: No. Everything happens in your browser and nothing leaves your device.

extract-pdf-images.title: Extract images from a PDF
extract-pdf-images.description: Download every image in a PDF at its original quality: photos as the original JPG and the rest as PNG, in a ZIP.
extract-pdf-images.about: Extract images pulls the photos, logos and illustrations out of a PDF so you can use them on their own: catalog photos, slides’ pictures or a report’s charts. It isn’t a screenshot of the page: you get each image at its original resolution. Images repeated on several pages are downloaded once.

faq.q1: Do the images lose quality?
faq.a1: No. Photos stored as JPG inside the PDF are copied byte for byte; the others are decoded and saved as PNG, which is lossless.
faq.q2: Why aren’t the text or drawings included?
faq.a2: Only images are extracted. Text and vector drawings (lines, tables, many logos) aren’t images; to keep them, use PDF to JPG, which converts the whole page.
faq.q3: What about a scanned PDF?
faq.a3: Each scanned page is an image, so you’ll get one image per page at the scan’s resolution.
faq.a4: No. Everything happens in your browser and the file never leaves your device.

markdown-to-pdf.title: Markdown to PDF
markdown-to-pdf.description: Turn Markdown (with tables, task lists and code) into a well laid out PDF, in A4 or Letter.
markdown-to-pdf.about: Markdown to PDF turns your notes, READMEs or documentation written in Markdown into a PDF ready to print or send. It supports GitHub flavor: tables, strikethrough, task lists and code blocks. Headings, lists and tables are laid out with readable margins and type, and links keep working inside the PDF.

faq.q1: Which Markdown elements are kept?
faq.a1: Headings, bold, italics, lists (including task lists), tables, quotes, code blocks, links and horizontal rules, in GitHub flavor (GFM). The PDF title is the first level-1 heading.
faq.q2: Are images included?
faq.a2: Only those embedded in the Markdown itself as data URLs (data:image/png;base64,…). Images linked from the web or from files on your computer are not downloaded: their alt text is shown instead. That way the server never reaches external addresses.
faq.q3: What happens to HTML written inside the Markdown?
faq.a3: For safety only its text is kept: tags, scripts, styles and iframes are removed before the PDF is made.
faq.q4: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: Yes: the PDF is made on our own server (not a third-party service), over an encrypted connection, and the file is processed in memory without being stored. If you'd rather nothing leaves your device, use Markdown to HTML and print the page as PDF from your browser.

html-to-pdf.title: HTML to PDF
html-to-pdf.description: Turn an HTML file into a PDF that keeps its styles, tables and embedded images, in A4 or Letter.
html-to-pdf.about: HTML to PDF prints saved web pages, email templates, invoices or exported reports as a PDF ready to send. Styles written inside the file (style tags and attributes), tables and images embedded as data URLs are kept. If the HTML sets its own page size with @page, that size is used.

faq.q1: Can I convert a web page from its address (URL)?
faq.a1: No: you upload or paste the HTML file. For safety our server never visits internet or internal addresses while making the PDF.
faq.q2: Why are some images or styles missing?
faq.a2: Only what is inside the file is used: styles in style tags or attributes, and images embedded as data URLs. Linked stylesheets, fonts and images (link, src or url() pointing to another file or site) are not downloaded.
faq.q3: Does the page's JavaScript run?
faq.a3: No. Scripts, event attributes, iframes, objects and redirects are removed before printing; you get what the page shows without JavaScript. Pages that build their content with JavaScript will come out incomplete.
faq.q4: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: Yes: the PDF is made on our own server (not a third-party service), over an encrypted connection, and the file is processed in memory without being stored.

pdf-to-pdfa.title: PDF to PDF/A
pdf-to-pdfa.description: Convert a PDF to the PDF/A archival format (1b, 2b or 3b) for long-term storage or official submissions.
pdf-to-pdfa.about: PDF to PDF/A turns your PDFs into the long-term archival format required by many public agencies, courts and universities. PDF/A embeds every font, pins colors to a profile and stores the metadata inside the file, so the document looks the same many years from now. The result is checked with the veraPDF reference validator.

faq.q1: Which PDF/A version should I choose?
faq.a1: Unless you are asked for another, PDF/A-2b: it is the most widely accepted and supports transparency and modern compression. PDF/A-1b is for older systems that only accept the first version; PDF/A-3b also allows files attached inside the PDF (e-invoices, for example).
faq.q2: Does the document's appearance change?
faq.a2: Content and pages stay the same. Some details may vary: fonts are embedded and, in PDF/A-1b, transparency is flattened. Links and interactive forms may be lost because the archival format does not allow them.
faq.q3: Can I convert a password-protected PDF?
faq.a3: No: PDF/A does not allow encryption. Remove the password first with “Remove a PDF password” and then convert it.
faq.q4: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: Yes: the conversion runs on our own server (not a third-party service), over an encrypted connection, and the file is processed in memory without being stored.

spreadsheet-converter.title: Spreadsheet converter
spreadsheet-converter.description: Convert between Excel (XLSX, XLS), OpenDocument (ODS) and CSV: every sheet, value and formula, in your browser.
spreadsheet-converter.about: Convert spreadsheets between Excel (XLSX and the older XLS), OpenDocument (ODS, from LibreOffice) and CSV or TSV. Turn a CSV exported by some system into an Excel file ready to work with, or an Excel file into CSV to load into another app. When reading a CSV the separator is detected and numbers with a decimal comma are recognized; when writing one you can choose comma or semicolon so that Excel in other languages opens it correctly.

faq.q1: What is kept?
faq.a1: Every sheet, the values (text, numbers, dates) and formulas with their last result. Visual formatting is not kept: colors, fonts, borders, column widths, charts and images.
faq.q2: Why does Excel show broken accents or everything in one column?
faq.a2: Excel in many European and Latin American languages expects a semicolon separator and a decimal comma. Choose “Semicolon” and keep UTF-8 with BOM checked so accented letters display correctly on double-click.
faq.q3: What happens to a workbook with several sheets when converting to CSV?
faq.a3: A CSV holds one table, so one CSV is made per sheet (with the sheet name in the file name), or only the first sheet's if you uncheck the option.
faq.a4: Up to 50 MB per file and 2 million filled cells, because everything is processed in your browser's memory. Your files are not uploaded to any server.

create-archive.title: Create ZIP
create-archive.description: Put several files in one ZIP, TAR or TAR.GZ in your browser, without uploading them to any server.
create-archive.about: Bundle several files into one to email them, upload them to a form or keep them together. Choose ZIP, the format Windows, macOS, Android and iPhone open without installing anything, or TAR and TAR.GZ, the usual ones on Linux and servers. You can choose how much to compress: photos, videos and Office documents are already compressed and are stored as they are, so no time is wasted; text, PDF and other files do get smaller.

faq.q1: Which format should I pick: ZIP, TAR or TAR.GZ?
faq.a1: ZIP if you're sending it to other people: any computer or phone opens it. TAR.GZ is the standard on Linux and for uploading files to a server. TAR only bundles the files without compressing them.
faq.q2: Why is the ZIP almost as big as my files?
faq.a2: Photos (JPG, PNG, WEBP), videos, audio and Office documents are already compressed inside, so compressing them again doesn't make them smaller. To make photos lighter, use “Compress image” before creating the ZIP.
faq.q3: Are names with accents or Chinese characters kept?
faq.a3: Yes. Names are stored in UTF-8, as current programs expect. If two files have the same name, the second becomes “name (1)”. Slashes in names are replaced so nothing can be written outside the folder when extracting.
faq.q4: Is there a size limit? Can I add a password?
faq.a4: Everything is built in your browser's memory, so the files can add up to 500 MB in total. Password-protected ZIPs aren't available yet: to protect a document, use “Password protect a PDF”.

extract-archive.title: Extract ZIP
extract-archive.description: Open ZIP, RAR, 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ and GZ files in your browser and download what's inside, with its folders.
extract-archive.about: Open an archive without installing any program: handy on a phone, a work computer or a tablet. You see the list of files it holds and can download each one separately or all together in a ZIP with the same folders. Works with ZIP (including ones made by older Windows versions, with accented names), RAR (versions 4 and 5), 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ/TGZ and GZ. The archive is opened on your device: it isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Is it safe to open a ZIP someone sent me?
faq.a1: It is opened as a potentially hostile file: nothing is run, paths that try to leave the folder (like “../”) are fixed, symbolic links and special files are skipped, and “zip bombs” stop once they pass the limit. Still, scan programs downloaded from unknown sources with an antivirus.
faq.q2: Which formats can it open?
faq.a2: ZIP, RAR (4 and 5), 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ (or TGZ) and GZ. Password-protected archives can't be opened here yet, nor ZIPs using unusual compression methods or RARs split into parts. In 7Z files, accented letters or other scripts in names may be replaced with “_”; the content doesn't change.
faq.q3: Is there a limit?
faq.a3: The archive can be up to 500 MB (RAR and 7Z up to 250 MB), and its contents up to 500 MB and 5,000 files in total, because everything is extracted in your browser's memory.
faq.a4: Yes: each file shows its path, and downloading everything together creates a ZIP with the same folder structure. Empty folders are not included.

image-to-text.title: Image to text (OCR)
image-to-text.description: Extract text from photos, screenshots and scanned documents with OCR, in your browser, without uploading the images.
image-to-text.about: Turn the text in an image into editable text: a photo of a document, a screenshot, a receipt or a scanned page. Choose the language of the text (Spanish, English, Portuguese, French or Chinese) for more accurate recognition. Everything happens on your device: the OCR engine and the language are downloaded once from our site and your images are not uploaded to any server. You get one .txt file per image, which you can also copy directly.

faq.q1: How accurate is it?
faq.a1: With sharp, straight printed text it usually gets almost everything right. Blurry, tilted or dark photos and handwriting give worse results; when confidence is low we warn you to check the text.
faq.q2: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a2: No. Recognition runs in your browser. Only the OCR engine and the chosen language model (about 2 to 4 MB) are downloaded the first time, from our own site.
faq.q3: Which formats and languages are supported?
faq.a3: JPG, PNG, WEBP, BMP, GIF, TIFF, HEIC and AVIF, up to 50 MB per image. Languages: Spanish, English, Portuguese, French and Simplified Chinese. Choose the language the text is written in.
faq.q4: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
faq.a4: If your PDF is a scan, use “OCR scanned PDF”: it recognizes every page and gives you a searchable PDF or a .txt file.

ocr-pdf.title: OCR scanned PDF
ocr-pdf.description: Turn a scanned PDF into a PDF with text you can search and copy, or extract its text, in your browser.
ocr-pdf.about: A scanned PDF is just a picture of each page: you can't search for a word or copy the text. This tool recognizes the text of each page with OCR and adds it as an invisible layer over the original page, which doesn't change: the PDF looks the same, but now you can search, select and copy. You can also get only the text as a .txt file. Pages that already have digital text are left as they are. Everything is processed on your device.

faq.q1: Does the PDF look different?
faq.a1: No. The original pages are kept as they are (same quality, same size); the recognized text is added on top, invisible, in the same position as the words in the image.
faq.q2: How many pages can it process?
faq.a2: Up to 100 pages and 100 MB per PDF. Each page is recognized in your browser and takes a few seconds, so a long document can take several minutes.
faq.q3: What about pages that already have text?
faq.a3: With the option checked they are left as they are, and their text goes into the .txt unchanged. Uncheck it if a page has only a little digital text (a stamp, for example) besides the scan.
faq.q4: Are my documents uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: No. The PDF is opened, read and recognized in your browser; only the OCR engine and the language model are downloaded once from our site.

epub-converter.title: EPUB Converter
epub-converter.description: Convert EPUB books into one HTML page or plain text (TXT), with images and a table of contents. In your browser.
epub-converter.about: Turn an EPUB ebook into a single HTML file that opens in any browser, with the cover, a table of contents, the chapters in order and the images included, or into plain text (.txt) to read it on any device, search it or copy from it. Works with DRM-free EPUB 2 and EPUB 3 books. Links between chapters keep working inside the page. The book is opened on your device: it isn't uploaded to any server.

faq.q1: Does it work with books bought with DRM?
faq.a1: No. EPUBs protected with DRM (Adobe, Readium LCP, Apple) are encrypted and can only be read in the store's app; the tool tells you so. DRM-free EPUBs work: public domain books, books from DRM-free publishers or ones you made.
faq.q2: Is the HTML it makes safe?
faq.a2: Yes. Scripts, event handlers, forms and javascript: links are removed, and the page carries a security policy that blocks loading anything from the internet: images are stored inside the file. The book's stylesheets aren't used; the page has its own reading styles, light and dark.
faq.q3: What is lost in the conversion?
faq.a3: The book's styles (fonts, colors, margins), audio, video and external images. Plain text keeps paragraphs, headings, lists (with dashes) and tables (cells separated by tabs).
faq.a4: Up to 100 MB per book and 300 MB unpacked, because everything is processed in your browser's memory. You can convert several books at once and download them in a ZIP.

epub-to-pdf.title: EPUB to PDF
epub-to-pdf.description: Convert EPUB books into PDFs ready to print or read on any device, with a table of contents and images.
epub-to-pdf.about: Turn an EPUB ebook into a PDF with the cover, a table of contents, each chapter starting on a new page and the images included, in A4 or Letter size. Handy to print a book, read it on a device that can't open EPUB or share it with someone without an ebook reader. Works with DRM-free EPUB 2 and EPUB 3 books. The book is opened in your browser and only the assembled page (without scripts) is sent to our server to print it; it's deleted when done.

faq.q1: Does it work with books bought with DRM?
faq.a1: No. EPUBs protected with DRM (Adobe, Readium LCP, Apple) are encrypted and can't be read outside the store's app; the tool tells you before sending anything.
faq.q2: Is the book's layout kept?
faq.a2: Text, headings, lists, tables, images and links between chapters are kept, with a reading layout of our own: each chapter starts on a new page. The book's fonts, colors and margins are not used.
faq.q3: What is sent to the server?
faq.a3: The book is read in your browser and turned into a single HTML page without scripts; only that page is sent to be printed as a PDF. On the server it is cleaned again, it can't load anything from the internet and it isn't stored: it's deleted when done.
faq.a4: The assembled page (with its images) can be up to 15 MB on the free plan and 50 MB with Pro. If your book has many images and goes over the limit, untick "Include the book's images".

create-epub.title: Create EPUB
create-epub.description: Turn Markdown or HTML into an EPUB book with a table of contents, chapters and images, ready for any reader. In your browser.
create-epub.about: Turn your Markdown or HTML texts into an EPUB 3 ebook that opens in Apple Books, Google Play Books, Kobo, Calibre and almost any reader. Each file is a chapter, in the order of the list, and within each one a new chapter starts at every main heading (# in Markdown, h1 in HTML). The table of contents is generated, images embedded in the file are included, and you can set the title, author and language. Everything happens in your browser.

faq.q1: How are chapters split?
faq.a1: Each file starts a chapter, in the order of the list, and within each file a new chapter starts at every main heading (# in Markdown or h1 in HTML). The table of contents is built from those headings.
faq.q2: What about images?
faq.a2: Images embedded in the file itself (data URLs in PNG, JPG, GIF or WEBP) are included in the book. Images linked to the internet or to other files can't be downloaded and are replaced by their alternative text.
faq.q3: Does it work on Kindle?
